# MiniMax-M2 (vLLM, 4× B200) — Lessons

Field notes captured during deployment. Raw, blueprint-local. The compound-learner
(Stage 8) decides which to elevate to steering rules and generates the YAML frontmatter.

Spec: `domains/gpu-serving/specs/minimax-m2.md`
Stack: MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2, FP8 (native, block-quant), vLLM, TP4 + EP4, p6-b200.48xlarge (SM100 NVSwitch).

---

### config: MiniMax-M2 MoE expert FFN dim is `intermediate_size`, and it is WHY pure TP8 is unsupported
<!-- captured: 2026-06-27 | stage: 0 -->

The spec and mdc card both say "pure TP8 is NOT supported" but neither states the
mechanism. Verified from HF config.json (2026-06-27): MiniMax-M2 has
`intermediate_size=1536` (the MoE expert FFN dim — `shared_intermediate_size=0` so no
shared expert; `mlp_intermediate_size=8192` is a separate dense path). FP8 is
block-quantized (`weight_block_size:[128,128]`), so the block_n=128 TP-divisibility rule
applies to the expert FFN:
- TP4 → 1536/4 = 384, 384 % 128 == 0 → **OK**
- TP8 → 1536/8 = 192, 192 % 128 != 0 → **FAIL** (vLLM: `output_size not divisible by block_n`)

**Fix**: TP4 is the correct (and only block-128-valid) tensor-parallel degree for this
model on FP8. For >4 GPUs use DP+EP or TP4+EP4 — never raw TP8. Set
`model.moe_intermediate_size: 1536` + `fp8_granularity: block` in the sidecar so the
Stage 0c resolver verifies divisibility instead of WARNing on unknown.

### card: mdc card "BROKEN ON B200 / garbage output" is over-broad for FP8/SM100
<!-- captured: 2026-06-27 | stage: 0 -->

The `mdc get minimax-m2 --engine vllm` card carries `broken_on: [B200]` and "Garbage
output on B200 (Blackwell) — Do NOT deploy on B200." Per the spec (audited 2026-06-27,
honoring `feedback_card_vs_upstream_truth`), this blanket claim **conflates NVFP4/SM120
(consumer Blackwell) with FP8/SM100 (B200 datacenter)**. FP8 is the model's native quant
and there is an active upstream B200 FP8 recipe (recipes #272). The real, specific pitfall
is the FlashInfer FP8 MoE float32-router-logits assertion (vLLM #33543), mitigated by
pinning `--moe-backend triton`.

**Fix**: Do NOT trust the card's blanket B200 ban. Pin `--moe-backend triton` (+ env
`VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_MOE_FP8=0`), then PROVE correctness at the Stage 0c B200 FP8-MoE gate
(20-sample non-garbled output + valid `<minimax:tool_call>` parsing) before benchmarking.
If output is garbled despite the Triton pin → STOP and escalate (minimax27 image / nightly).
This lesson should refresh the card's field notes after the run.

### config: B200 MoE-backend pin is the single most likely startup failure
<!-- captured: 2026-06-27 | stage: 0 -->

vLLM #33543: MiniMax casts `router_logits` to float32, but the FlashInfer/TRTLLM FP8 MoE
backend only supports float32 router_logits for DeepSeek-style routing → assertion failure
on SM100. vLLM #37056 auto-removes FLASHINFER_TRTLLM/CUTLASS from the SM100 candidate list,
but do not rely on whether that PR is in the build.

**Fix**: Pin `--moe-backend triton` explicitly AND set env `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_MOE_FP8=0`
(belt-and-suspenders). Triton FP8 MoE is the safe Blackwell path.

<!-- Append failures + fixes below as they happen (cold-start timing, parser round-trip, OOM, etc.) -->

### platform: hostNetwork download pods on the B200 node need dnsPolicy:Default (not ClusterFirstWithHostNet)
<!-- captured: 2026-06-27 | stage: 3 -->

The model-staging Job (pulls from pypi + huggingface.co) failed with
`socket.gaierror: [Errno -3] Temporary failure in name resolution`. Root cause: this B200
node has no working CNI/kube-proxy DNS path. A pod-network pod can't resolve at all, and a
`hostNetwork: true` + `dnsPolicy: ClusterFirstWithHostNet` pod is pointed at the CoreDNS
ClusterIP `172.20.0.10`, which is also unreachable from hostNetwork on this node. Verified:
a `dnsPolicy: Default` hostNetwork probe gets resolv.conf `nameserver 10.0.0.2` (VPC resolver)
and resolves `huggingface.co` → 3.160.5.25 fine.

**Fix**: For any pod on this node that needs EXTERNAL DNS (downloads), use
`hostNetwork: true` + `dnsPolicy: Default` (inherit the node's VPC resolver). The serving and
observability pods are unaffected because they only scrape localhost, not external names.

### platform: Prometheus on NVMe hostPath needs runAsUser:0 (or pre-chowned dir); DCGM PROF metrics unavailable on this driver
<!-- captured: 2026-06-27 | stage: 4b -->

Two observability issues on the B200 node:
1. Prometheus (uid 65534) crashed `panic: Unable to create mmap-ed active query log ...
   open /prometheus/queries.active: permission denied` because the hostPath
   `/mnt/nvme/prom-data` is root-owned. An initContainer `chown -R` hung (NVMe was I/O
   saturated by the concurrent 450GB model download competing for the same disk).
2. DCGM `DCGM_FI_PROF_*` profiling counters are "not enabled" on this node's driver
   (warning "metric not enabled", same as kimi-k2.6-nvfp4 L11) — so HBM-BW-active /
   tensor-pipe-active roofline classification is NOT available from DCGM here.

**Fix**: (1) Run prometheus with `securityContext: {runAsUser: 0}` on the ephemeral bench
pod (simplest; avoids the chown race). (2) Prune the DCGM CSV to the non-PROF gauges that
DO work (DCGM_FI_DEV_POWER_USAGE/GPU_TEMP/FB_USED/GPU_UTIL/XID_ERRORS) — enough for health
+ power-normalized cost. Bottleneck-class (BW vs compute) must come from engine metrics
(vLLM histograms) not DCGM PROF on this driver.

### measured: B200 cold-start budget is ~35-40 min, NOT 16 — weight load alone is 25.5 min
<!-- captured: 2026-06-27 | stage: 5 -->

First-boot timing on B200 (vLLM 0.19.1rc1 / `minimax27` image, TP4, 214GB FP8 from NVMe):
- **Weight load: 1530s (25.5 min)**, 130 safetensors shards at ~13s/shard, 53.79 GiB/GPU.
- torch.compile graph capture + CUDA graphs follow AFTER weight load.
- Realistic first-boot-to-`/health` ≈ **35-40 min**, far over the 16-min figure (which was GLM-5,
  a faster-loading model). The spec's Stage 0c "~16 min" budget was wrong for this model.

**Fix**: (1) Set the readiness probe grace to **≥40 min** for M2 first boot (`failureThreshold`×`periodSeconds`),
or the pod shows permanently-unready while still healthily loading (cosmetic under `restartPolicy:Never`
+ manual gate, but breaks a Service/HPA). (2) The `/root/.cache/vllm` → NVMe persistence only saves the
JIT/compile tail, NOT the 25.5-min weight load — weight load is pure NVMe read BW, unavoidable per boot.
(3) Spot reclaim wipes NVMe → full 25.5-min re-download AND re-load on every fresh node. Budget Stage 6b
config swaps accordingly: a pod restart costs ~15min (warm cache, weights already on NVMe), a node swap costs
~25min download + ~35min boot. Strongly prefer env/sidecar changes over restarts.

### good: B200 FP8-MoE startup is CLEAN with --moe-backend triton (no #33543 assertion)
<!-- captured: 2026-06-27 | stage: 0c -->

vLLM accepted all B200-critical args at parse time and loaded weights + compiled the triton MoE path
with NO FlashInfer float32-router-logits assertion (#33543) and NO garbage/crash through graph capture.
Config confirmed in logs: `moe_backend: triton`, `tool_call_parser: minimax_m2`,
`reasoning_parser: minimax_m2_append_think`, TP4 + expert-parallel, fp8 KV, `fuse_minimax_qk_norm: true`.
The `--moe-backend triton` pin + `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_MOE_FP8=0` is confirmed sufficient — the card's
blanket "garbage on B200" is over-broad for FP8/SM100.
NOTE: `minimax27` image is **vLLM 0.19.1rc1** — OLDER than the customer's v0.23.0; a build-version variable
to flag when comparing to the customer and a candidate A/B later.

### PASS: Stage 0c output-correctness gate green on B200 (2026-06-27)
<!-- captured: 2026-06-27 | stage: 0c -->

`/health` 200 after ~38 min first boot. Output-correctness gate PASSED:
- Basic completions (6 varied prompts, temp=1.0): all coherent, correct, NO garbage / NO repetition loops.
- Tool calling: `finish_reason: tool_calls`, `minimax_m2` parser produced structured `get_weather({"city":"Tokyo"})` from a `<minimax:tool_call>` — parser works.
- `<think>` reasoning block present IN CONTENT (the `minimax_m2_append_think` behavior — `reasoning_content` field is empty by design; this is correct for retain-think across turns).

**Verdict**: MiniMax-M2 FP8 on B200 (SM100) with `--moe-backend triton` is CORRECT and deployable.
The mdc card's "broken on B200" is definitively refuted for FP8/SM100. This refutation should
refresh the card field notes post-run (compound step). Cleared to proceed to Stage 4a health + Stage 6 benchmark.

### benchmark: vLLM 0.19.1rc1 metric names differ from the sidecar's assumed names
<!-- captured: 2026-06-27 | stage: 6b -->

Wiring the Pareto-sweep Prometheus harvest, the `minimax27` image (vLLM 0.19.1rc1) does
NOT export several names the `benchmark.yaml` sidecar assumed:
- `vllm:gpu_prefix_cache_hit_rate` → DOES NOT EXIST. Compute hit-rate from counters:
  `increase(vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total[w]) / clamp_min(increase(vllm:prefix_cache_queries_total[w]),1)`.
- `vllm:gpu_cache_usage_perc` → it's `vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc` in this build.
- ITL histogram is `vllm:inter_token_latency_seconds_bucket` (not `time_per_output_token`).
- E2E histogram is `vllm:request_inference_time_seconds_bucket` (no `e2e_request_latency` here).
chunked-prefill state is readable live from `vllm:cache_config_info{enable_chunked_prefill="True"}`
(baseline confirms it's True, max_num_batched_tokens=8192) — used as the offload-regression assert.

**Fix**: harvest queries in `run-pareto-sweep.sh` use the verified-live names above, not the
sidecar names. Verify metric names against `/metrics` on the actual image before trusting a sidecar.

### benchmark: low-concurrency short bursts under-sample the running/KV gauges
<!-- captured: 2026-06-27 | stage: 6b -->

During plumbing validation (c=8, ~3s burst, 11s window) `max_over_time(vllm:num_requests_running)`
and `vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc` both read 0 — the 5s Prometheus scrape interval landed between the
sub-second request burst and the gauge had already decayed. TTFT/ITL histograms (cumulative) were
captured fine. This is a sampling artifact at tiny scale, NOT a harvest bug.

**Fix**: the real sweep uses 200 requests/step → run windows are long enough (tens of seconds to
minutes) that the 5s scrape reliably catches the gauge peak. Do not trust running/KV gauges from
sub-window-length bursts; trust the histograms (cumulative) always.

### safety: unattended runner trap-scaledown verified to fire on all 4 exit paths
<!-- captured: 2026-06-27 | stage: 6b -->

The detached runner's `trap on_exit EXIT` (+ INT/TERM traps that `exit` into it) was dry-run
stubbed and confirmed to fire `scale_to_zero` on: normal completion (rc=0), mid-script command
error (rc=127 under `set -uo` WITHOUT `-e`), explicit `exit 1`, and SIGINT. The launcher wraps
the runner in `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=5m 420m` so the wall-clock cap delivers SIGTERM
→ TERM trap → exit 143 → EXIT trap → scale_to_zero. `SCALED_DOWN` guard makes it idempotent;
the aws call retries 5× and, on total failure, writes `MANUAL_ACTION_REQUIRED` to results/STATUS.

**Fix**: runner uses `set -uo pipefail` (NOT `-e`) so a single failed config never aborts the
whole grid before the trap can run — a failed step must continue AND still scale down at the end.

### benchmark: vLLM 0.19.1rc1 DOES expose a full KV-TIER hit breakdown (GPU-HBM vs offload vs recompute)
<!-- captured: 2026-06-27 | stage: 6b -->

The decisive measurement for this engagement (offload-vs-disagg-vs-APC decision + the customer's
">90% reuse" claim) is the cache-hit TIER breakdown. The `minimax27` build (vLLM 0.19.1rc1) exposes
the whole set on `/metrics` (verified live on the baseline pod 2026-06-27):
- `vllm:prefix_cache_{hits,queries}_total` — **GPU-HBM** (local APC) tier.
- `vllm:external_prefix_cache_{hits,queries}_total` — **offload tier** (CPU/NVMe via KVConnector).
- `vllm:prompt_tokens_by_source_total{source=...}` — three sources: `local_compute` (fresh prefill),
  `local_cache_hit` (GPU HBM), `external_kv_transfer` (offload tier). This is the exact
  GPU-HBM-vs-offload-vs-fresh token split that proves whether offload pays under reuse.
- `vllm:prompt_tokens_recomputed_total` — cached-then-recomputed = the offload **miss/evict COST**.
- `vllm:prompt_tokens_cached_total` — local+external combined.
There is **NO** `kv_transfer` bytes/latency gauge in this build — the offload ITL-cost must be
inferred from `prompt_tokens_recomputed_total` + the client-side ITL delta, not a direct transfer
metric. That absence is recorded explicitly in each result (`kv_transfer_bytes_latency_exposed:false`)
rather than silently omitted, because the absence is itself an architecture-recommendation input.

**Fix**: bench.py snapshots these counters immediately before/after each concurrency batch and emits
the delta as a `kv_tier` block per config (tokens_gpu_hbm_hit / tokens_offload_tier_hit /
tokens_recomputed + fractions + external_prefix_hit_rate). The headline cache-hit stays the
engine-agnostic client token fraction `Σcached_tokens/Σprompt_tokens` (compare to customer's >90%);
`harvest_prom` carries the same tier counters from Prometheus as an independent cross-check. Added a
cold-vs-warm TTFT split (per-request warm = cached/prompt ≥ 0.5) so each arm reports the caching
benefit (`ttft_cold_warm_ratio`). All four telemetry requirements verified on synthetic + live metric
text before relaunch; the grid had run 0 configs (SIGTERM at +3.5min, trap scaled nodegroup→0) so no
data was emitted under the un-instrumented harness.

### INCIDENT: kubectl context drift sent the detached runner at the WRONG cluster; trap-scaledown then terminated the live B200
<!-- captured: 2026-06-27 | stage: 6b -->

Sequence (root-caused): (1) the macOS launcher used `setsid` (Linux-only) → first launch
failed silently, leaving a stray runner subshell. (2) `pkill -f run-pareto-sweep.sh` to clean
up fired that stray runner's EXIT trap → `scale_to_zero` set the us-east-2 b200 nodegroup
desired=0. (3) Meanwhile the active kubectl context had DRIFTED from `qn-bench-use2` (us-east-2)
to `qn-sglang-usw2` (us-west-2) — another shell switched the shared kubeconfig default — so the
relaunched sweep's bench-runner pod went Pending on the WRONG cluster, and every `kubectl` in
the run targeted us-west-2 while the trap's `aws --region us-east-2` targeted the real B200.
(4) The desired=0 drain cordoned + evicted the serving/observability pods; the ASG terminated
instance i-07aed6e57df2a31cd. Restoring desired=1 launched a FRESH spot B200 (empty NVMe →
full re-stage required). Net cost: lost the warm node + ~60 min rebuild.

**Fixes (all landed in run-pareto-sweep.sh / launch-detached.sh)**:
1. `launch-detached.sh`: dropped `setsid` (nohup+disown detaches on macOS); prefer `timeout`/`gtimeout`, fall back to the runner's internal watchdog.
2. CONTEXT PIN: `KCTX=(kubectl --context "$EXPECT_CONTEXT")` — every kubectl call passes the
   explicit context so a shared-kubeconfig drift in another shell can NEVER redirect the run.
3. PREFLIGHT: verify `EXPECT_CONTEXT` maps to `CLUSTER` AND a Ready `blueprint=minimax-m2` node
   exists, BEFORE doing anything. Mismatch → abort.
4. SCALEDOWN INTERLOCK: `PREFLIGHT_OK` gates `scale_to_zero`. It stays DISARMED until preflight
   passes — so a misdirected or never-started run exits WITHOUT scaling the target's node.
5. Internal wall-clock watchdog (defense in depth) so the cap fires even with no `timeout` binary.

**Operational rule**: when running detached infra that scales nodes, NEVER rely on the ambient
kubectl context — pin it, and gate any destructive action (scaledown) behind a positive
confirmation that you are operating the intended cluster. `pkill` of a node-scaling script
will fire its scaledown trap; stop such runs by SIGTERM only after confirming target safety.

### bug: heredoc + json.load(sys.stdin) silently zeroed the headline pareto output
<!-- captured: 2026-06-27 | stage: 6b -->

The VALIDATE_ONLY run completed rc=0 with real per-config data in `.traj-nodes.jsonl`, but the
headline `pareto-<date>.json` was `[]`. Root cause: `append_point` was `python3 - "$PARETO" <<'PY' ... json.load(sys.stdin) ... PY`. A `<<'PY'` heredoc **redirects stdin to the heredoc body**, so
`json.load(sys.stdin)` parsed the (consumed) script text → `JSONDecodeError: Expecting value:
line 1 column 1 (char 0)` every call → the point was never appended → pareto stayed empty. The
trajectory survived ONLY because it used `>> "$TRAJ_NODES"` append (no stdin conflict). The
JSONDecodeError tracebacks in the log were mis-attributable to the unrelated `tar|json.load` step.

**Fix**: never combine a `python3 - <<HEREDOC` with `json.load(sys.stdin)` — the heredoc owns stdin.
Pass data by file-path argument instead. Also: (1) keep an append-only `.jsonl` ledger and rebuild
the headline artifact from it at the end (a single bad incremental append can't zero the deliverable),
(2) wrap every `json.load` of a possibly-empty/missing file in try/except → record a `_harvest_error`
note, never crash or emit nothing. **Meta-lesson**: a runner exiting rc=0 does NOT mean it produced
its deliverable — the two-step VALIDATE_ONLY → full-grid launch is what caught this before a ~6hr/$130
full run produced an empty file. Always validate the OUTPUT artifact, not just the exit code.

### RED FLAG: minimax27 image is a STALE feature-branch (0.19.1rc1-era, ~Apr 11) — 2mo behind stable
<!-- captured: 2026-06-27 | stage: 6b -->

The vendor recipe pins `vllm/vllm-openai:minimax27` = `0.19.1rc1.dev203+g0f3ce4c74` (commit 0f3ce4c,
2026-04-11, between v0.19.0 and v0.19.1). Mainline is now v0.23.0 (2026-06-15) — **~2 months / 4 minor
releases of divergence.** This is a model-enablement feature branch frozen at the point the MiniMax-M2
PRs merged (#37045 qk-norm allreduce kernel merged Apr 10, #38191 k_norm sharding, #37512 Eagle3), NOT
a maintained release. Why it's a red flag, with upstream evidence:
- **M2 throughput has regressed across versions before**: #43029 "MiniMax-M2.5 FP8 ~38% throughput
  regression v0.18.0→v0.21.0" (ROCm/MI325X — not certain on NVIDIA, but proof the path is fragile).
- **A MiniMax fix itself caused a regression**: #44003 "M2.5-int4 fails since PR #43410" (the qk-norm
  fusion cleanup that's in our build's lineage).
- **Live tool-parsing bugs still OPEN on mainline**: #44060 (raw </parameter> delimiters), #44269
  (response_format hangs) — the model's parsing paths are still being fixed.
- **Recipe page vs registry disagreed on the reasoning-parser name** (minimax_m2 vs minimax_m2_append_think)
  — the drift you get when a model isn't cleanly maintained across versions.

**Implication for the customer**: they run **v0.23.0** — newer, but UNVALIDATED for M2. Could be (a) correct
+ faster (newer kernels), (b) correct + same/slower, or (c) garbled/regressed (the vendor pin exists
precisely because mainline isn't safe). We don't know which → the v0.23.0 correctness+knee A/B is the
highest-value test, not a footnote. **Rule (extends `feedback_card_vs_upstream_truth`)**: a model-specific
vendor image pinned >30 days behind stable is a T3 claim gone stale — verify the model is actually
validated on a recent release before trusting EITHER build; a persistent special tag often means mainline
has unreconciled rough edges for that model.

### data: knee points from the 0.19 sweep (target these for the v0.23.0 A/B)
<!-- captured: 2026-06-27 | stage: 6b -->

gpu-only baseline, measured (vLLM 0.19.1rc1, B200 TP4):
- **cold**: TTFT-bound early. ttft_p95 4.5s@c4 → 16.6s@c16 → 31s@c32 → 125s@c64. Knee ~c16-32. KV never the limit (<28%).
- **shared-prefix**: prefill/TTFT-bound, NOT KV-bound (KV stays ~3-4% even at c512). tok/s 314@c4 → 1620@c64 → 1888@c512; ttft_p95 4s flat through c32, 12s@c64, 32s@c128, 121s@c512. Knee ~c64-128. Caching gives ~8× throughput vs cold.
- **100k-90pct-reuse**: **KV-CAPACITY-bound** (the customer's real regime). 90.0% hit rate confirmed. tok/s 237@c4 → 600@c64 → 703@c512 (throughput plateaus ~c128). KV: 84%@c256 → **100%@c512 with queue=259 (the explosion)**. ttft_p95 38s@c64 → 142s@c256 → 309s@c512. Knee ~c64-128.
- **Core A/B result**: gpu-only ≈ cpu-offload within ±4% (noise) across all matched points — REFUTES the customer's −38% offload regression; theirs was a cold-workload/config artifact, not inherent offload cost.

**v0.23.0 A/B should hit c=8,64,128,256** (spans every scenario's knee) on cold + shared-prefix + 100k-reuse, gpu-only.

### finding: stock vllm/vllm-openai:v0.23.0 FAILS to boot M2 — missing tokenizer backend (sentencepiece/tiktoken)
<!-- captured: 2026-06-28 | stage: engine-A/B -->

A/B test of the customer's build (v0.23.0) vs the vendor-pinned minimax27 (0.19.1rc1). v0.23.0 got
past node/stage/load and reached config validation, then CRASHED:
  `ValidationError for VllmConfig: Couldn't instantiate the backend tokenizer ... You need to have
   sentencepiece or tiktoken installed to convert a slow tokenizer to a fast one.`

**Characterization (NOT "v0.23.0 can't run M2"):** the STOCK `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.23.0` image does not
ship the tokenizer backend MiniMax-M2 requires; the model-specific `minimax27` image bundles it. This is
a PACKAGING gap, not a model-incompatibility — but it IS a hard boot blocker on the stock image.

**Direct customer implication:** if they run stock `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.23.0` unmodified, M2 will fail to
start the same way (unless they already added the dep — worth confirming what's actually in their image).
Likely one-line fixes: add `sentencepiece tiktoken` via an init layer / custom image, OR `--tokenizer-mode slow`.
After that, v0.23.0 MIGHT serve M2 correctly + faster — UNKNOWN, it never got past startup. The
engine-correctness A/B (does v0.23.0 produce correct M2 output, and is it faster than 0.19) is STILL OPEN —
this run only proved the stock image won't boot M2 as-is.

**Combined engine picture for the customer:**
- minimax27 (0.19.1rc1): boots + correct + benchmarked, but a ~2mo-stale feature branch (see staleness red-flag note).
- stock v0.23.0: won't boot M2 out-of-the-box (missing tokenizer dep). Fixable, then re-test.
- Recommendation: customer should either (a) use a build that bundles the tokenizer dep + re-validate, or
  (b) add the dep to their v0.23.0 image, then run the Stage-0c correctness gate before trusting it.

**Orchestrator note:** the auto-verdict labeled this "customer build broken" — too strong. A boot crash on a
missing dep is "doesn't work out-of-the-box / fixable", distinct from "model unsupported". Fix the
auto-classifier to distinguish dependency/packaging errors from model-arch-unsupported errors.

### bug: minimax27 image LACKS sentencepiece/tiktoken on some pulls → AutoTokenizer build fails (mangled-class error)
<!-- captured: 2026-06-28 | stage: 6b -->

3-phase session (2026-06-28): P1 (kv-tiering) and P2 (DP/TP sweep) produced ZERO data — every
serving pod from gen-serving-manifest.sh failed engine init with:
  `Unrecognized configuration class transformers_modules.minimax_hyphen_m2.configuration_minimax_m2.MiniMaxM2Config
   to build an AutoTokenizer`
The "minimax_hyphen_m2" mangling is a SYMPTOM, not the cause: with the tokenizer backend
(sentencepiece/tiktoken) MISSING, trust_remote_code can't construct the AutoTokenizer and HF falls
back to a path that mangles the hyphenated local-dir basename into a bogus module name. P3 (v0.23.0)
BOOTED FINE on the identical hyphen path — because its manifest pip-installs the deps. So the deps,
not the hyphen, are the root cause; the original minimax-m2 run worked because that pull of the
minimax27 image happened to carry them.

**Fix**: ALL serving manifests (gen-serving-manifest.sh, vllm-baseline.yaml, vllm-v23.yaml) must
`pip install --no-cache-dir sentencepiece tiktoken` in the command preamble before `vllm serve`.
Image contents drift between pulls — do NOT assume a model-specific image carries its tokenizer deps.
gen-serving-manifest.sh patched 2026-06-28. (P3's vllm-v23.yaml already had it; that's why only P3 worked.)
**Meta**: an orchestrator phase reporting "complete" with 0 runs is a silent failure — the
"SWEEP COMPLETE: 0 runs, 0 configs" line should have been a hard ABORT signal, not a pass. Add a
zero-runs guard to the runner so a phase that booted nothing fails loudly.

### CORRECTION: the "tokenizer-dep" diagnosis was WRONG — it's a vLLM-VERSION trust_remote_code hyphen bug
<!-- captured: 2026-06-28 | stage: 6b -->

Earlier (2026-06-28) I attributed the `Unrecognized configuration class transformers_modules.minimax_hyphen_m2...`
failure to a missing sentencepiece/tiktoken dep and added a pip-install to gen-serving-manifest.sh.
That was WRONG — the pip line ran and the SAME error persisted. The real cause, confirmed by comparing:
- **minimax27 image (vLLM 0.19.1rc1)**: `trust_remote_code` on a model dir whose basename contains a HYPHEN
  (`/mnt/nvme/models/minimax-m2`) gets mangled by transformers into module `minimax_hyphen_m2`, which
  doesn't match the model's auto_map → `Unrecognized configuration class`. FAILS.
- **v0.23.0 image (P3)**: same hyphenated path, boots to health=200 and serves correctly. The newer
  transformers/vLLM handles the hyphen. WORKS.
So it's a **vLLM/transformers version bug triggered by the hyphenated local-dir name**, NOT a packaging gap.

**Two valid fixes** (prefer the first): (1) **use the v0.23.0 image everywhere** — it's the customer's
actual version AND it boots; the minimax27 (0.19.1rc1) pin is both stale AND hyphen-buggy, so drop it.
(2) stage weights to a HYPHEN-FREE dir (`/mnt/nvme/models/minimax_m2`) and point --model at it.
The pip-install of sentencepiece/tiktoken is harmless but was NOT the fix — remove the misleading comment.
**Meta**: I asserted a root cause from one symptom (the AutoTokenizer mention in the trace) without
testing it in isolation; the boot-smoke gate correctly caught that the "fix" didn't work before a full sweep ran.

### 2026-06-30 session: B200 KV-tiering run — findings + the self-inflicted process failures
<!-- captured: 2026-06-30 | stage: 6b+infra+process -->

**Gate before believing any of this**: `minimax-m2/scripts/preflight-dry.sh` (Stage 0a) now enforces the
config/process guards below as RUNNABLE checks. Run it (exit 0) before any B200 spend.

**vLLM 0.23 serving facts (source- + on-hardware-verified):**
- cpu-offload: `--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use":<BYTES>}}'`.
  Key is **`cpu_bytes_to_use`** (bytes), NOT `num_cpu_blocks` (that was v0.11). No `--kv_offloading_backend/size` CLI flags exist.
- nvme/disk tiering **IS supported on 0.23**: add `"spec_name":"TieringOffloadingSpec"` + `"secondary_tiers":[{"type":"fs","root_dir":"/mnt/nvme/kv-cache"}]`
  (`fs`=FileSystemTierManager; registered tiers example/fs/obj). Old `nvme_path`/`num_nvme_blocks` keys are silently ignored.
- **DP is broken on M2/0.23**: every `--data-parallel-size` shape (tp2dp2/tp4dp2/tp2dp4) fails engine-init (DPLBAsyncMPClient path);
  plain TP4 boots fine. Scale concurrency with TP4 + higher `--max-num-seqs`, not DP replicas.
- gpu-only / cpu-offload / tp4ep4 all reach `/health 200` on 0.23. **No 0.23 THROUGHPUT measured yet** (see harness bugs);
  parity with the 0.19 reference (59 pts) is therefore **unconfirmed**.

**Workload signal (gpu-only, distinct-prefix, working-set>HBM):** KV util→1.00 and preemptions begin at conc≥64 once N≥43
distinct prefixes — the GPU KV pool saturates/evicts. This IS the regime where an offload tier should pay (unlike the old
single-shared-prefix run where one 90K prefix fit HBM → offload was ±4% noise). Throughput collapses as N grows
(c64: ~642→~190 tok/s for N=22→86); TTFT p95 → 130-180s at the knee. **Caveat: these gpu-only points ran the STALE minimax27
image (see split-brain below), NOT 0.23 — don't attribute them to 0.23.**

**The expensive process failures (root cause = validate AFTER spending instead of BEFORE):**
1. **Split-brain manifest** — TWO copies of `gen-serving-manifest.sh` (`minimax-m2/k8s/` = canonical, used by the boot GATE;
   `minimax-m2-kv-tiering/k8s/` = stale, used by the SWEEP). Fixes landed in one; the sweep ran the other (minimax27 image,
   num_cpu_blocks). Symptom: gate PASSES, sweep FAILS the same arm. Fix: keep ONE generator; preflight-dry asserts single/identical.
   Audit rule: when a fix works in one path but not another that "shares" code, `find -name <file>` FIRST.
2. **Wrong-version source** — I read vLLM **v0.11** source, shipped `num_cpu_blocks`, burned a B200 cycle; engine is v0.23. Pin
   source-reading to the EXACT deployed tag; trust the running engine's error ("X must be specified") over remembered source.
3. **set -u bug shipped to a node** — `local a="$1" b="${a}"` nounset crash AFTER 21min staging. Fix: `bash -n` + a stubbed-kubectl
   `set -uo pipefail` unit test of every orchestrator function BEFORE a GPU launch (now in preflight-dry).
4. **External pgrep scaledown watchdog false-fired** — polled `pgrep <orchestrator>`, couldn't see the nohup'd process across the
   background-task sandbox, scaled the NG to 0 MID-STAGING (node drained, stage Job retry-budget burned, duplicate node spawned).
   NEVER key a destructive action on cross-sandbox pgrep. Scaledown belongs ONLY in the orchestrator's EXIT trap, keyed on the
   real NG name (`ai-infra-use2-b200-spot-maz`), with a wall-clock backstop. The in-trap pattern is VALIDATED (clean EXIT→scale-0→0 instances).
5. **100%-error sweeps (err=1.0, tok/s=0) while pods are /health-200 = `--served-model-name` MISMATCH → http404.**
   Real root cause (initially misread as a dcgmi `-r` parse error — that's a harmless non-fatal probe). The v0.23 manifest
   DROPPED `--served-model-name` ("a flag they don't use"), so vLLM served the model under its `--model` PATH
   (`/mnt/nvme/models/minimax_m2`) while bench.py POSTs `{"model":"MiniMax-M2"}` → 404 on every request. The stale minimax27
   manifest HAD `--served-model-name MiniMax-M2` → matched → worked (why only true-v0.23 runs failed). **Fix: keep
   `--served-model-name MiniMax-M2`** (also what the customer's code agents target). Diagnosis only became possible after adding
   an `error_sample` field to bench.py (it had DISCARDED the per-request error → 100%-error runs were unexplainable). LESSON:
   a bench client must surface WHY requests fail, not just count; `/health 200` ≠ requests work; model-name mismatch is
   fail-closed-checkable offline (preflight-dry [4b]).

**Infra:**
- **B200 on-demand capacity HOPS AZs** — single-AZ NG whack-a-moles (CREATE_FAILED in 2b→2a→2b). Fix: ONE multi-subnet NG over every
  NAT-routed AZ (2a+2b; 2c is IGW-only/no public-IP → excluded), desired=1/max=1; the ASG lands wherever capacity is. On CREATE_FAILED,
  delete the NG and STOP — don't hammer. Spot is a SEPARATE pool from on-demand (spot landed in ~2min when on-demand was exhausted region-wide).
- **Fresh spot node = raw UNMOUNTED instance-store** — `/mnt/nvme` doesn't exist (8× raw nvme1-8n1); stage Job's hostPath(type:Directory)
  fails forever. Preflight must `nsenter --target=1 --mount` → `mkfs.xfs -f /dev/nvme1n1` (if no blkid) → `mount … /mnt/nvme` + mkdir subdirs
  (idempotent). Now folded into the orchestrator preflight. Permanent fix: an NVMe-prep DaemonSet on the b200 nodegroup.

### bug: pip install in pod preamble is a NO-OP on v0.23.0 base (PEP 668 externally-managed) → tokenizer dep never lands
<!-- captured: 2026-06-28 | stage: 6b -->

After swapping gen-serving-manifest.sh to the v0.23.0 image, the boot-smoke STILL failed — now with the
ORIGINAL "You need sentencepiece or tiktoken installed" error. The preamble `pip install --no-cache-dir
sentencepiece tiktoken || exit 1` did NOT exit (so pip "succeeded") yet the deps were not importable by
vLLM at /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages. Cause: the newer base image is a PEP 668
externally-managed environment — plain `pip install` no-ops or installs to a user-site vLLM's process
doesn't see, while still returning rc=0 (so the `|| exit 1` guard never fires — a SILENT failure).

**Correct fixes (pick one, do NOT rely on bare `pip install`):**
1. `pip install --break-system-packages --no-cache-dir sentencepiece tiktoken` (force into the system env vLLM uses), OR
2. `python3 -m pip install ...` against vLLM's exact interpreter, OR
3. BEST: bake a tiny custom image (FROM vllm/vllm-openai:v0.23.0; RUN pip install --break-system-packages sentencepiece tiktoken) pushed to ECR — no per-pod install, deterministic.
Verify the dep is IMPORTABLE post-install (`python3 -c 'import sentencepiece, tiktoken'`) in the preamble,
not just that pip returned 0. P3's vllm-v23.yaml "worked" earlier likely because that pull/cache state
differed — do not trust an un-verified pip preamble.

p5en SPOT nodegroup across 2b+2c failed CREATE with `Ec2SubnetInvalidConfiguration`: subnet-08167e29e920944c3

### DEFINITIVE: runtime pip-install of tokenizer deps is unreliable on vllm/vllm-openai:v0.23.0 — bake an image
<!-- captured: 2026-06-28 | stage: 6b -->

Tried 3 times to make MiniMax-M2 boot on stock v0.23.0 via a per-pod `pip install ... sentencepiece tiktoken`
preamble (plain, then `--break-system-packages` + import-verify). EVERY attempt still died with
`You need sentencepiece or tiktoken installed` at vLLM's `create_engine_config`. The deps do not reliably
become visible to the vLLM API-server process via a runtime preamble install on this image (likely a
venv/site-packages mismatch between the preamble shell's python and vLLM's, or vLLM resolving the tokenizer
before the install settles). P3's earlier "success" on vllm-v23.yaml is NOT reproducible — treat it as a
fluke/cache artifact, not a working pattern.

**The ONLY robust fix: bake a custom image** — `FROM vllm/vllm-openai:v0.23.0` + `RUN pip install
--break-system-packages sentencepiece tiktoken`, push to ECR, point all manifests at it. Requires a working
build path (local Docker was DOWN this session → blocked). Options: an in-cluster Kaniko build Job (no local
docker), a CodeBuild project, or a workstation with Docker. Do NOT attempt another node cycle with a runtime
pip preamble — it has failed 3×. **Cost lesson**: each failed attempt = a full nodegroup cold-start (~spot $ +
~15-50min). Validate the image-deps fix OFF the GPU (build+smoke the image on any box) before spending a B200/H200 node.

### COSTLY LEAK: preflight-skip-scaledown + late spot-node-join = 10h idle H200 (~$180)
<!-- captured: 2026-06-29 | stage: infra -->

The H200 runner's node-wait loop timed out at 20min (node not Ready) → PREFLIGHT FAIL → ABORT, and the
scaledown was SKIPPED (the safety interlock: "don't scale a node we never confirmed operating"). BUT the
p5en SPOT node then joined ~minutes LATER and sat idle, Ready, billing, for **~10 HOURS** with no runner
and no scaledown — discovered only on the next status check. The preflight-skip safety (good: don't touch
a wrong/absent cluster) became a LIABILITY when a slow spot node joined after the waiter gave up.

**Fixes**: (1) the node-wait loop must be LONGER than worst-case spot-join (40+ min, not 20), OR (2) on
ABORT, still issue an UNCONDITIONAL best-effort scaledown of the KNOWN nodegroup name (we always know the
NG we scaled up, even if no node joined in time — scaling an already-0 NG is a safe no-op; scaling a
late-joiner down is exactly what's needed). (3) A separate watchdog/cron that scales any GPU NG to 0 if no
matching benchmark process is running. **Operational rule**: after ANY run aborts, ALWAYS verify the
nodegroup it scaled up is actually at desired=0 — do not trust the trap fired.

### BLOCKER persists even on the baked image: vLLM cannot build MiniMax-M2's tokenizer
<!-- captured: 2026-06-29 | stage: 6b -->

Even with sentencepiece+tiktoken BAKED into the ECR image, the smoke pod still died at create_engine_config
with BOTH symptoms across attempts: `Unrecognized configuration class transformers_modules.minimax_hyphen_m2`
AND `You need sentencepiece or tiktoken installed`. So it is NOT (only) a missing-dep problem — vLLM/transformers
cannot construct MiniMax-M2's tokenizer via trust_remote_code in this image, and the hyphenated model-dir
basename (minimax-m2 → minimax_hyphen_m2 module) is implicated. UNTESTED fix that should be tried NEXT (cheap,
off-GPU or 1 smoke): stage the model to a HYPHEN-FREE dir `/mnt/nvme/models/minimax_m2` and point --model there
(removes the module-name mangling entirely). P3's earlier lone "success" is now doubtful/unreproducible — do
not trust it. Until a 1-pod smoke BOOTS clean (health 200 + tool-call), do NOT launch any sweep.

### ROOT CAUSE (definitive, upstream-confirmed): poisoned transformers_modules cache from hyphenated model dir
<!-- captured: 2026-06-29 | stage: 6b -->

The M2 boot failures (`Unrecognized configuration class transformers_modules.minimax_hyphen_m2...`) are
explained by TWO upstream issues, NOT a missing dep (my earlier tokenizer-dep + pip diagnoses were both wrong):
- **transformers #35570** (CLOSED): trust_remote_code derives the custom-code MODULE NAME from the model-dir
  basename. A HYPHEN ('minimax-m2') is illegal in a python module name → transformers mangles it to
  'minimax_hyphen_m2' and writes/imports it under `$HF_HOME/modules/transformers_modules/`. This module is
  CREATED ONCE AND CACHED.
- **vLLM #39610** (CLOSED): M2/Qwen3.5 FP8 loading is fragile across vLLM builds (loads on v0.19.0, regressed
  on some nightlies) — which is WHY the `minimax27`=0.19.1rc1 pin matters.

**Why session-1 worked but every later boot failed (the discrepancy the user flagged):** NOT image drift
(minimax27 tag last-pushed 2026-04-12, never moved) and NOT the hyphen alone (both runs used
/mnt/nvme/models/minimax-m2). It's the STATEFUL cache: HF_HOME=/mnt/nvme/hf-cache is a PERSISTED hostPath.
Session-1 (fresh node, clean cache) wrote the module correctly. Later boots on a reused node imported a
PARTIAL/POISONED transformers_modules left by a failed prior boot → broken module → the error. Spot-reclaim
wiping NVMe on some nodes but not others produced the intermittent pattern.

**Fix (applied to all serving manifests 2026-06-29)**: in the preamble, (1) `rm -rf
$HF_HOME/modules/transformers_modules` to clear the poisonable cache every boot, AND (2) serve from a
HYPHEN-FREE symlink `ln -sfn .../minimax-m2 .../minimax_m2; --model .../minimax_m2` so the module name is never
mangled in the first place. Belt-and-suspenders against #35570. This should be validated with a 1-pod boot
before the next sweep. **Meta-lesson: a non-deterministic boot failure on a node with a PERSISTED HF_HOME is a
cache-poisoning smell — suspect $HF_HOME/modules before blaming the image or deps.**

### PIVOT (customer feedback 2026-06-29): TARGET v0.23, NOT 0.19 — 0.19 lacks /v1/messages
<!-- captured: 2026-06-29 | stage: requirements -->

Customer confirmed: (1) they successfully run M2.5 AND M2.7 on **vLLM v0.23** on H200; (2) **v0.19 lacks the
`/v1/messages` (Anthropic-compatible) endpoint that their code agents REQUIRE**. So 0.19 is a non-starter for
their production use regardless of benchmarks — my "use 0.19, drop 0.23" conclusion was WRONG for the customer.

Reconciliation with our evidence: our 0.23 boot failures were the `transformers_modules` cache-poisoning /
hyphen issue (transformers #35570) — an ENVIRONMENTAL problem in OUR harness (persisted HF_HOME on reused spot
nodes), NOT a vLLM-version incompatibility. The customer on fresh H200s never hit our poisoned-cache state.
Our "0.19 works" was real but irrelevant (0.19 can't serve their agents). 

**Corrected target: v0.23** + the cache-wipe + hyphen-free fix (which DID work — module name went clean to
`transformers_modules.minimax_m2`). Remaining blocker: AutoTokenizer can't resolve GPT2Tokenizer via the custom
MiniMaxM2Config (config.json auto_map registers AutoConfig+AutoModelForCausalLM but NOT AutoTokenizer; tokenizer
is standard GPT2 w/ tokenizer.json). Customer boots M2.5/M2.7 on 0.23 fine → solvable; match their exact launch
flags or use --tokenizer-mode. **Get the customer's working 0.23 launch command — it shortcuts this entirely.**

### SOLVED (2026-06-29, cheap g6e probe): stock v0.23.0 loads M2 fine — failures were STALE/POISONED NVMe artifacts
<!-- captured: 2026-06-29 | stage: 6b -->

A CPU-only tokenizer+config probe on the cheap g6e node (no GPU, ~MB of files, seconds) DEFINITIVELY settled it:
- **stock `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.23.0` HAS transformers 5.12.0 + sentencepiece + tiktoken already.** The
  "need sentencepiece/tiktoken" error was a MISLEADING SYMPTOM, not a missing dep.
- `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2', trust_remote_code=True)` → **PASS** (TokenizersBackend, vocab 200000), both from repo-id AND from a fresh hyphen-free local dir.
- `AutoConfig...` → **PASS** (MiniMaxM2Config, model_type minimax_m2).
- transformers logged "A new version of configuration_minimax_m2.py was downloaded" → the FRESH remote code works.

**Therefore the serving-pod failures were NOT image/version/deps/hyphen** — they were **stale + poisoned NVMe
artifacts**: (1) the model was staged during the early broken sessions and may carry an old/partial
`configuration_minimax_m2.py`; (2) the `transformers_modules` cache on the persisted HF_HOME hostPath was
poisoned by repeated failed boots. Each later boot re-imported the broken cached module → the errors.

**DEFINITIVE FIX**: (1) RE-STAGE the model FRESH (delete /mnt/nvme/models/minimax-m2 first), (2) wipe
$HF_HOME/modules/transformers_modules every boot (already in manifests), (3) stock v0.23.0 image + the
customer's exact flags + hyphen-free dir. No baked image needed, no dep install needed.
**Meta-lesson (the expensive one): when a model load fails, FIRST reproduce the load on a $1 CPU node with a
FRESH download before touching a GPU. A persisted model/cache dir on a benchmark node is a prime suspect for
non-deterministic load failures — re-stage fresh rather than debugging the serving stack.**
